text:
mike: quick follow-up from today's postmortem — we need concrete owners + timelines for the rollout/feature-flag changes we discussed. goal: stop the same blast-radius pattern repeating. can people pick items? :memo:
tara: I can own the short-term canary size reduction and manual rollback playbook. will draft steps tonight and PR tomorrow morning. :+1:
aditya: I will wire the anomaly detector into the rollout service so it can trigger auto-rollback on defined signals. target: EOW. I'll post the signal thresholds for review.
sophia: we should add explicit traffic-split stages and a kill-switch. sketch of config we talked about:
```json
{
  "stages": [
    {"pct": 1, "duration_min": 30},
    {"pct": 5, "duration_min": 60, "auto_rollback_on": "latency>500ms || error_rate>2%"},
    {"pct": 20, "duration_min": 120}
  ],
  "kill_switch": true,
  "max_concurrent_canaries": 3
}
```
this enforces gradual ramp + explicit rollback conditions.
chris: I'll add per-tenant flag gating for top-10 enterprise customers so we can exclude them from risky rollouts until verified. ETA 2w.
olivia: I'll update the runbooks (rollout checklist) and add synthetic load steps: long-seq, KV-miss, and retry storms. i'll also add a checkbox to verify prefix-KV caching behavior in the smoke.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated for r-2025-10-14-42 by @mike (stage: 1 -> 1% traffic)
mike: important recurring pattern from postmortems — latency spikes correlate with long-sequence requests that miss the KV cache and cause big CPU spikes on the runtime. we need a synthetic test harness that forces long-seq + cold-cache scenarios pre-rollout. who can own that?
aditya: I'll expand the CI canary suite to include a long-seq/cold-cache job. ETA next Wednesday.
tara: action items summary (I'll track in the tracker):
- A1: shrink default canary sizes + update rollout policy (owner: tara, ETA: +24h)
- A2: integrate anomaly detector into rollout service (owner: aditya, ETA: EOW)
- A3: staged traffic config + kill-switch enforcement (owner: sophia, ETA: 72h)
- A4: per-tenant gating for enterprise accounts (owner: chris, ETA: 2w)
- A5: synthetic long-seq / cold-cache tests in CI (owner: aditya, ETA: next Wed)
- A6: runbook + smoke checklist updates (owner: olivia, ETA: 3 days)
please comment if any ETA is unrealistic. i'll add these to the postmortem follow-up board.
aditya: for A2 I propose these signals to trigger rollback: p95 latency > 400ms sustained for 1 minute, error_rate > 1.5% over 1 minute, token-generation-timeout spikes. will post exact query.
sophia: add a soft-rollback first (reduce to previous stage) before full rollback to limit false positives — we can have a two-step auto-response: step1 shrink traffic to 0.5% (10m), step2 full rollback if metric persists.
mike: agree. also add a limit on concurrent canaries (sophia's config includes that). we should also throttle model-heavy routes during ramp (e.g., seq_len > 1024 get sampled).
chris: noting dependencies: per-tenant gating requires small flag infra change + UI so CS can opt-in. i'll open the ticket today and sync with product.
olivia: i'll schedule a 30m sync for Friday 09:00 to validate the canary plan before we push infra changes. ping here when PRs are up.
deploy-bot: Canary aborted automatically at stage 2 for release r-3454 due to latency spike (p95=812ms) — rollback executed by auto-policy.
mike: that abort shows the auto-rollback path works, but we lost visibility in the middle. action: add better tracing for canary bit and surface a single dashboard with metric deltas. (owner: olivia, ETA: 5 days)
tara: I'll also add a short manual-playbook for oncall: how to detect, when to hit kill-switch, and communication templates for customers. will link to the board.
aditya: one more ask: make the anomaly detector outputs visible in the rollout UI (signal and reason text) so oncall can understand why rollback happened. (owner: aditya, ETA: EOW)
mike: thanks folks. please update the follow-up board with the specific GitHub PR links when you have them. i'll reconvene Friday @ 09:00 to close items A1/A3/A6 if ready. :calendar:
